chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who rents a house and then rents it out for more than he rented it for, he said: 'That is not permissible unless he adds something to it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a person to legally sub-lease a rented property for a higher price in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the validity of sub-leasing (*ta'jir*), a common commercial practice in early Islamic society. The Imam stipulates that mere arbitrage is insufficient; rather, the sub-lessor must introduce a tangible improvement or addition to the property to justify the markup, thereby preventing unjust enrichment and ensuring fairness in transactions. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on value addition (*ziyadah*) as a prerequisite for legitimate profit in lease agreements.
